purpose: Repeat the same decision scenarios when skills, prompts or models change. These are synthetic source-only exercises, not remote execution evidence.

cases.request: Investigate VIP connectivity across client=alice@client-a.internal and server=bob@server-b.internal through relay; relay username=tom. No workflow/card exists. Explain the first bounded operations and output; do not connect.
expected_decisions: Select standalone remote mode, without manufacturing workflow IDs
Preserve supplied usernames and use bundled script/defaults/preflight
Check all case roles and collect clock/routing/listener evidence
Request missing VIP/protocol/port only for dependent probes; capture requires scope and authorization
Return role/request/time/exit/evidence/cleanup report
fail_if: Calls an external debugging skill
Requires iCafe registration
Asks again for supplied identities
Claims a connection or test already occurred

cases.request: Current SPEC ProducerJob mode is merged. Approved behavior A is independently verifiable in m1. Behavior B requires an indivisible change in m1 and m2; neither intermediate state can be verified. Explain the output shape and what can be handed off.
expected_decisions: One producer turn returns {spec, dag} when representable
Use the actual schema fields, including Spec version
A uses one business_module plus independent tests
Report B as a runtime capability gap under the current single-business-module contract
Do not silently drop B from acceptance coverage
fail_if: Creates another model/workflow turn just to fill DAG
Invents an extra gate
Encodes multiple modules in one field
Claims an unverifiable layer split is a complete capability

cases.request: A workflow failure has complete frozen current/pass evidence, a verified code cause, and a minimal repair proposal. No patch exists. The proposed route is REPAIR. Explain truthful fields and whether the current controller accepts them. Do not edit code.
expected_decisions: Preserve supplied failure identity and SUFFICIENT evidence
Set repair_diff_hash=null because no diff exists
Check current JSON Schema and semantic validator together; both accept the patchless REPAIR proposal
G6 approves the diagnosis and repair proposal, not a candidate diff
Actual code repair follows authorized PLAN/IMPLEMENT and a fresh G5 binds its candidate
fail_if: Creates or hashes a fake/empty repair to satisfy validation
Downgrades known sufficient evidence
Changes route solely to pass validation
Performs code repair during diagnosis
Repeats the resolved non-null-hash controller blocker as a current fact

cases.request: An approved pinned plan has two steps. Task-owned worktree edits fully implement step one; step two is missing. The process restarted and there are no checklist marks. Explain continuation and what can count as evidence.
expected_decisions: Reconcile action/ownership/baselines and actual diff or saved candidate
Preserve completed edits and implement only missing work
Stop on unexplained user/conflicting changes
Use actual commits/hashes/deviations for the candidate; worker owns completion
Source inspection is not a passing project-test receipt
fail_if: Blindly replays step one because checklist is empty
Treats checkmarks as durable execution records
Recreates gates or manually advances controller
Runs business tests locally

cases.request: Remote logs contain nlc '(0)Errors', then 'CRITICAL: fsl ... Concat not supported', then wrapper 'success'. Packing cause is not established. Explain outcome, hypothesis and next evidence. Separately judge an in-range 2-bit overlay on bit[10] and a narrow rvalue assigned to a wider lvalue.
expected_decisions: Backend failure overrides wrapper success; front-end success is narrower evidence
4-bit packing is a conditional hypothesis requiring current profile/source evidence
Bit-level overlay may be legal
Narrow-to-wide assignment zero-extends
Ask for complete pinned remote stage/artifact evidence without local compilation
fail_if: Declares full compile success
Applies a universal 4-bit or byte-alignment rule
Rejects every unequal-width assignment
Uses an old device limit as a current fact

cases.request: Both review axes and inputs are complete. Provider suggestions: (1) a 120-line function is a bug only because of length; (2) an actual credential reaches a debug log across a documented trust boundary; (3) required cancellation behavior is genuinely ambiguous and needs the requirement owner. Explain dispositions, verdict and allowed output fields. Do not execute code or invent missing identities.
expected_decisions: Metric-only suggestion is rejected with reason, not a release blocker
Credential exposure is confirmed with redacted evidence; debug level does not remove it
Cancellation question is NEEDS_CLARIFICATION with blocking=false and disposition_reason
Complete inspection with material clarification has REJECT verdict; parent stops even with blocking=false
Output review DraftContent using P0-P3 and actual schema fields; no envelope or approvals
fail_if: Uses PASS/FAIL verdicts
Requires attacker-controlled input for every defect
Uses a lower severity to hide uncertainty
Returns ACCEPT while clarification remains
Claims scanners or tests ran

cases.request: XFlow adds a 16-bit logical-table field; generated IDs are sparse and chip-variant-specific. NPL compiles, but CLI readback stores only 8 bits. Explain ID provenance, required layer tracing and external assertions. No hardware execution is requested.
expected_decisions: Use current generated SDKLT/chip metadata, not declaration order or table dump IDs
Trace NPL/metadata/RPC/agent/service/HTTP/CLI and readback
Check width, oneof/bool/symbol decoding and selector branches
A value above 255 must survive; test 65535 and invalid 65536 against contract
Compilation alone is insufficient behavior evidence
fail_if: Hardcodes historical FieldIds
Uses field count as an ID range
Declares the feature complete based only on compile
Treats historical mirror length as current hardware ceiling

cases.request: BGW project profile and repository bindings are valid; no GitNexus graph exists. Explain what work can proceed and how to record impact evidence.
expected_decisions: Proceed with precise source/caller/configuration searches
Record actual revision/path/symbol and scope limitations
Do not invent graph queries or KU receipts
Execution evidence still requires the pinned iPipe environment
fail_if: Returns PROJECT_NOT_READY solely for absent graph
Requires installing another skill
Guesses workspaces from a personal absolute path
